To supply boiler-feed water to CHP and LP boiler de-mineralized (DM) water plant has been envisaged. Separate cooling towers are considered for direct cooling and indirect cooling circuit. Wastewater of the plant will be coming out from two sources. i. As effluent water from De-mineralized (DM) water plant ii. As a blowdown from the cooling towers 2.0 Water for Demineralized (DM) Plant The total DM water requirement for the project will be approx. 925 GPM. DM water will be required to generate steam in the WGS unit and power plant. The makeup water quality as received from the plant is furnished below (Table 2). This water will be used as feed water for the reverse osmosis (RO) based DM plant and makeup for the cooling water system. Table 2: Make-up Water Quality Sl. No. Parameter Unit Value A. Reactive Silica (as SiO ) mg/L 1.3 2 The following scheme is envisaged to convert makeup-grade water into DM-grade water. A pretreatment facility using a dual media filter shall be installed to remove suspended solids (TSS) & Turbidity. Inlet TSS (Total suspended solid) is considered ten ppm (approx.) for designing the filtration system, as the water test report does not specify any suspended solid or turbidity. An ultrafiltration system can also be considered before the RO unit as an alternative to a Dual media filtration system. After pretreatment, filtered water shall be fed to the Reverse osmosis (RO) system to remove dissolved Attachment-3: Wastewater Treatment Study 4 DE-FE0031937 / 0004 solids from the water. A necessary dosing system shall be considered before the RO system to prevent it from scaling and fouling. After RO, a degasser tower will be used to arrest the dissolved CO present in the 2 RO permeate and to maintain the pH to a neutral level of the permeate. Then the degassed water will be fed to the mixed bed unit for final polishing, where any slippage of dissolved solids & reactive silica from the RO system is trapped. The outlet of the RO-MB system is called DM quality water
